source.title: How to Mitigate Overfitting in Weak-to-strong Generalization?
source.authors: Junhao Shi; Qinyuan Cheng; Zhao-Ye Fei; Y. Zheng; Qi-Peng Guo; Xi-Peng Qiu

page_placements.theme: Weak-label quality and predictors of W2S outcome (self-consistency, sample reward, step-error severity, supervisor variance, error similarity, intrinsic dimension)

record.file_problem: Text is substantially complete. Some figures are flattened or lack readable point values; the paper also notes that the MATH evaluation subset has 500 items and provides an additional 5,000-item evaluation for Deepseek.
record.tranche_reason: It runs weak-label fine-tuning and reports performance gap recovered, including conventional weak-to-strong baselines, on new model series and tasks. The confidence filtering and relabeling stages are additional interventions.
record.gate_note: Rows cover reported PGR results, comparisons of the proposed training stages with conventional weak-to-strong fine-tuning, ablations, and the no-chain-of-thought comparison. Figure 3's label-accuracy trend and the difficulty/topic-distribution analyses are not PGR or weak-to-strong task-performance results. Related-work results cited from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study runs conventional weak-to-strong fine-tuning (weak instruct/chat model labels, base student, gold-trained ceiling) and reports PGR. It does this on new settings: chain-of-thought math reasoning (GSM8K, MATH) with Llama 3 and Deepseek, plus SciQ with Qwen using the original protocol. It then tests a training change, confidence filtering plus strong-model relabeling, against naive fine-tuning. This bears on V1, V2 and, through one student-size comparison, V3. The theory in Appendix C.1 restates Lang et al. (2024) and is not the study's own test of V5. Nothing bears on V4 or V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors add that chain-of-thought supervision is needed for weak-to-strong gains on reasoning tasks: without it, students underperform weak teachers. They also report PGR reaching or exceeding 100% on some settings and claim the approach generalises to SciQ classification.
record.recipe_differences: The conventional baseline follows weak-label fine-tuning and uses the original PGR measure, but evaluates mathematical reasoning and SciQ with instruct/chat weak models. The paper adds confidence filtering, Stage II relabeling, and chain-of-thought settings not part of the basic comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: PGR changes with dataset/model, confidence threshold, Stage I versus Stage II, whether Stage II labels are filtered, and chain-of-thought versus direct-answer supervision.

fits_no_version.finding: Raising the weak model's self-consistency threshold raises label accuracy (Fig 3). It also lowers training-set difficulty (average level 3.48→2.66) and topic diversity (Counting & Probability 10.79%→4.31%) (Figs 5, 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Confidence filtering of weak labels trades label accuracy against the difficulty and diversity of the training questions.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates or significance tests are reported. The authors note that their initial MATH evaluation used a 500-item subset and that threshold choice varies across tasks; they provide a 5,000-item Deepseek evaluation as an additional check. Some numerical descriptions in the text and tables are inconsistent, including the chain-of-thought comparison.
record.rows_left_out: The full threshold sweeps and many Stage I/Stage II combinations in Appendix Tables 6-9 exceed the 60-row cap when combined with the other separately reported results. Kept conventional baselines, representative high-performing configurations, pronounced declines or reversals, and the Stage II filtering ablation; omitted the remaining threshold/configuration rows from Appendix Tables 6-9 and most configurations in Appendix Table 4.

untested.parts: Auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling of weak supervisors, and loss variants. Only data filtering/relabeling and CoT-vs-direct supervision are tested.
Representations or other predictors of PGR; controlled scaling of supervisor or student size (math uses one pair per series); chess and reward modelling.

Everything: exploitation of what the supervisor can't check, PGR under train/test distribution shift, and correlated weak/strong errors. The threshold-induced shift in the training set is the method's own choice.
No original theory; Appendix C.1 restates Lang et al. (2024) bounds.
No vision or other non-language modality.

missing.what: Deepseek MATH Stage I at thresholds 60/70/80% gives PGR 53.66/60.98/43.90%, below naive (65.85%). The 70% threshold used elsewhere is below naive here.
Llama 3 MATH Stage I at 30% gives PGR equal to naive (36.17%). Several Stage II combinations (e.g. 60%+50%: 34.04%) are at or below naive.
An extra iterative relabeling round (Stage Exp) on Deepseek reaches PGR 93.08% (GSM8K) and 134.15% (MATH).

record.verdict_notes: Weak supervisors are instruct/chat models, while students and ceilings are base models, which differs from the original setup. Best thresholds are chosen from sweeps evaluated on the test sets, with no validation split stated, so the peak PGRs are optimistic. No uncertainty is reported; MATH500 has 500 items, and the authors note up to 0.2 points per item. The main text and tables disagree (Llama MATH baseline accuracy 18.2 vs 27.2; Qwen-14B Stage II gain 8.3 vs 3.1). Table 3's caption says Deepseek, but its CoT numbers match Llama 3, and its direct-answer PGRs do not all follow from its own numbers.

versions.untested_parts: No safety-specific task or weak/strong models beyond the tested mathematical and SciQ settings.
The paper tests uncertainty filtering, relabeling discarded questions, and chain-of-thought prompting; it does not test auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling weak supervisors, or other loss variants.
Tests several model sizes/series and tasks, but does not test what representations predict PGR. Size comparisons are not a controlled scaling study.

Tests performance changes with filtering-induced changes to the training-question distribution. It does not test naturally occurring distribution shift or whether weak and strong models' errors are alike.
Provides a theoretical argument under stated expansion, error, and robustness conditions; it does not empirically test those conditions.
No vision or other non-language modality is tested.

rows.stage_stated: theoretical
rows.operation_detail: Derives error bounds for weak-label learning on covered and uncovered sets

conditions.value: expansion conditions, bounded weak-teacher error, low weak-label error, and robustness on uncovered data

rows.measure: Bound on student true error relative to weak-teacher error
rows.value: The paper states that under the stated expansion and low-error/robustness conditions, the student's true error can be lower than the weak teacher's.
